text: Access per graph: its owner, accounts with write access, and who may add notes
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: whoever creates a graph owns it. Write access can be granted to accounts. What guests may do is configured by the server admin or even per graph: making offers, and maybe making notes, which would be like creating issues on GitHub. Creating a graph on a server needs that permission for the account.

Guests are accounts without rights on a graph, including automatic accounts.

Replaces the roles of today's hosted mode, which apply to the whole server (read, write, admin in access.ts). Rights are per graph, not per idea: the owner and accounts with write access may change everything in the graph; everyone may read.

Offers and notes themselves (the guest layer) are ideas b7e0b972 and 34b3d747.

Unchanged from 2026-11-10: write access never allows starting a terminal or an agent on the server.

Assumed by Claude, not said by Felix: the server admin sets the defaults and the owner of a graph may change them for that graph; a mirrored graph has no writers on the server.

status.comment: Planned 2026-11-12 at Felix's request; nothing built.
